claim: The proposed `Reflect → Compound → Scout ⇢ Observe` topology requires a backward FSM transition that does not exist and an Observe ingestion channel that does not exist.
evidence: `phaseFSM` exposes only Current/Advance/IsTerminal; Advance() increments an index into a fixed `phaseOrder` and errors with `cannot advance past %s` at Compound (phase.go:39-49); there is no SetPhase or rewind. Observe's entire gate map is `read, glob, grep, ls` (registry.go:50-52) and `Tools(phase)` returns only gated tools (registry.go:165-177), so a scout report can re-enter Observe only by being written into the workspace — the same read surface as ground-truth source. Failure: appending PhaseScout after PhaseCompound moves IsTerminal one phase late while the Compound-gated quality-signal write (agent.go:246-253) still cuts the durable artifact before Scout runs.

claim: Scout reaches the leading-candidate slot on a trigger — 'unresolved contradiction, or detected shear' — that has no referent in any state record the loop carries, and the charter never requires triggers to be decidable.
evidence: Verified grep: the charter (and files derived from it) are the only hits for 'shear' in the repo — no detector, field, or event. `agent.Evidence` carries phase, turn, tool calls, tokens, stop reason, outcome, complexity, budget; `mutations.QualitySignal` carries task type plus hard/soft/human rate scalars. Neither can express 'two beliefs conflict'. Only 'validated mechanism' has a referent (a Compound write). Failure: with no state predicate the trigger degrades to model self-report, so the operation is neither schedulable nor auditable and a missed Scout is indistinguishable from a correctly skipped one.

claim: None of the eight tournament criteria asks which edge or state variable disappears when the candidate box is deleted, so a candidate already realizable as an existing phase-gated capability can win a phase contest.
evidence: Outward search already exists as an Orient-gated capability: `web_search`/`web_fetch` are registered for {Orient, Decide, Act} and `tierForPhase` spends the `deep` Exa tier in Orient and `instant` in Act — Skaffen has already encoded an exploration/exploitation gain schedule on one tool. `RegisterForPhases` (registry.go:136-153) is the entire implementation cost. Failure: the tournament crowns a winner whose real diff is one RegisterForPhases call plus a prompt, while charter:117 reports it as a new loop element with a confidence figure, and the team pays acronym, doc, gate-map and Intercore role-map cost for an unchanged transfer function.

claim: Scout's triggers surface in Orient/Reflect but its gate sits after Compound, adding a full cycle of deadtime — and the phase it occupies has no search tools at all.
evidence: Compound's gate map is `read, glob, ls, bash, edit(manifest globs), write(manifest globs)` — no web_search, no web_fetch — while Orient (where the trigger arises) has the deep-tier search. Compound is also where the session's durable artifact is cut (agent.go:246-253), so a post-Compound box writes after the artifact it would influence. Failure: over weeks, lateral search fires one cycle late on every contradiction-triggered case, probes address stale conditions, and the measured probe-success rate argues against S for the wrong reason (placement, not merit).

claim: The charter asserts agent orchestration is an orthogonal topology, then seeds Share — a candidate whose entire content is a change to that topology — so either Share is out of scope by construction or the axiom is false and untested.
evidence: Share adds no loop state and no authority; it adds an edge between loops owned by different agents. Skaffen takes the axiom seriously — `agentloop` is deliberately phase-agnostic so multi-agent scenarios need not carry OODARC (PHILOSOPHY.md:19), and `SelectionHints.Phase` is optional precisely because non-phased consumers exist. Failure: Share is scored on the same eight O/O/R/C-relative criteria, loses on semantic distinctness against Compound, and is eliminated — discarding the one candidate that would have falsified the axiom.

claim: The one sentence carrying the review's entire empirical burden names no measured quantity, threshold, cycle count, recorder, or outcome that would favor the no-S null, so the tournament cannot lose and the required confidence figure is unearned.
evidence: charter:119 reads in full 'A minimal read-only pilot for the top two choices plus the no-S null.' Every other required output (113-118) is argumentative; this is the only place the world gets a vote, and as written it can only demonstrate that the candidate ran — consistent with the candidate being valuable, worthless, or harmful. charter:94 applies falsifiability to candidates but never to the decision. Failure: the review ships at 'moderate confidence'; weeks later someone reports the scout reports were 'interesting', with no null arm and no pre-registered threshold — and the letter is now in the acronym, making reversal a naming migration.

claim: A 'read-only' pilot is unachievable in this runtime: every candidate turn writes the evidence file that Compound aggregates into the very QualitySignal a pilot would use as its outcome measure — a confounded design.
evidence: Every turn emits agent.Evidence to the per-session JSONL and best-effort bridges it to intercore under `agent_name: skaffen` (feeding Interspect routing calibration). At Compound, `mutations.Aggregate` reads every line and folds it into the session's QualitySignal, computing token efficiency, turn count and tool-error rate indiscriminately; the lightweight `evidenceRecord` decoder ignores unknown fields, so any tag a scout turn carried is dropped before aggregation. Failure: cheap, error-free scout turns inflate token efficiency and dilute the error-rate denominator, so the pilot concludes S improved quality when it only changed the mix — or exploratory web_fetch failures inflate ToolErrorRate and Interspect down-weights the agent for exploration it was instructed to perform.

claim: 'Only successful probes may be Compounded' is a selection rule on the wrong variable: it rewards predictions that were never at risk and erases the failed probes that carry the information.
evidence: A prediction's value is its severity — the prior probability it fails. A success-only gate makes the optimal strategy to emit near-certain predictions restating mechanisms the team already believed. Failed probes ('this source domain is barren') are discarded, so no base rate for transfer success and no failure attribution to a source domain is ever computable. Skaffen already keeps negative results elsewhere: `ExperimentEvent` retains Decision/Delta for rejected autoresearch mutations, and `BestApproach` reasons over accumulated signals, so base rates are the unit this system already thinks in. Failure: after a quarter the store holds forty successful, unsurprising transfer lessons and a 100% probe-success rate that reads as productivity, with no one able to answer which domains were tried and found barren.

claim: Retirement is specified as a field the artifact carries about itself, with no actor, clock, or sweep that consumes it — and one coarse 'speculative' grade leaves nothing for a sweep to write even if one existed.
evidence: Verified: `grep -rni 'authority|speculative|provenance'` over internal/ returns zero hits; the only expire/TTL machinery is the 15-minute web-search cache and interlock file reservations — nothing retires a claim. `authority: speculative` collapses 'mechanism validated in an adjacent domain with a working correspondence map' and 'surface analogy noticed once' onto one rung, so there is no defined transition to raise or lower an artifact. Failure: scout reports accumulate as epistemic debt — each marked speculative, none retired — until a reader finds a two-year-old correspondence mapping with a confident prediction and no sign its review condition passed unobserved.

claim: Six of eight criteria are phrased as properties of an operation, so no-S scores N/A on most of the matrix; and no output item asks which evidence discriminates between hypotheses, so non-diagnostic evidence will read as support.
evidence: Semantic distinctness, operational crispness, generativity, falsifiability, mnemonic/taste and pace fit all presuppose an operation; 'no S' wins only complexity cost, and no scoring rule for the null is given. Evidence likely to be cited — 'cross-domain transfer sometimes produces good ideas', 'Orient does not currently search laterally on purpose' — is consistent with Scout, Speculate, a capability, and the null alike. Failure: the null scores 1/8, the winner 6/8, and the recommendation reports high confidence on a result determined by criterion phrasing before any evidence was weighed.

claim: Scout, Search, Speculate and Synthesize share one (input, output, consumer) contract and differ only in which facet of the act they name, so the shortlist can rank a single operation three times while calling it a competitive field.
evidence: Input: a validated mechanism or anomaly. Output: a lower-authority transfer hypothesis with a correspondence mapping. Consumer: a later Observe/Orient turn deciding whether to probe. Search names the behavior, Scout the behavior plus its report artifact, Speculate the epistemic status, Synthesize the output shape. The charter's own probes ('Scout vs Speculate') presuppose these are rivals; if the contracts are identical the probe returns a naming preference dressed as a finding — the exact failure charter:100 records from the prior run. Failure: three of four shortlist slots hold one operation while retirement, pre-action counterfactual, and cross-agent propagation are never scored.

claim: Scout matches this codebase's definition of a capability on every property that distinguishes it from a phase — conditional, unpositioned, artifact-emitting — so the phase claim is carried by the acronym rather than the contract.
evidence: In Skaffen a phase is a member of `phaseOrder` the FSM walks through and a key in `defaultGates` scoping tool authority — positional and unconditional. A capability is a tool bound to phases via RegisterForPhases, fired at the agent's discretion, emitting an artifact another phase consumes. Scout is 'conditional, not mandatory each cycle' (47), emits a report consumed by Observe (41): three for three on capability. Organizational-learning research agrees — absorptive capacity and transfer-of-practice are modelled as capabilities exercised within existing stages. Failure: as a capability the change is one RegisterForPhases call plus a prompt, reversible in an afternoon; as a phase it is a new phaseOrder member, defaultGates entry, Intercore role-map change, TUI rendering, the acronym in every doc, and a migration to undo.

claim: Sensemake restates Orient with a widened quantifier and Select restates Compound's admission test, inflating the longlist whose diversity is the review's stated deliverable.
evidence: 'Sensemake — build a broader frame from accumulated evidence' vs Orient's 'interpret evidence in the current context and choose a useful frame'; 'Select — choose what deserves promotion' vs Compound's 'promote validated lessons'. Neither can be sorted from its neighbour by a practitioner given only the one-liners; the boundary requires the charter's prose to adjudicate. Failure: a nine-entry longlist reads as a thorough search when two entries are existing phases renamed and four are one operation, so confidence in coverage is calibrated to a word count.

claim: Six required source domains, only S-word seeds, a criterion rewarding pronounceable verbs, and no output item asking for the mechanism-first name — so a mechanism search is silently converted into a word search and the substitution cost is never declared.
evidence: The mechanisms those domains actually yield do not start with S: control theory gives dither / probe injection / model-reference adaptation; ecology gives forage / drift / disperse; intelligence tradecraft gives collection tasking / RFI; falsification gives severe test; organizational learning gives absorb / boundary-object exchange. Each will arrive wearing an S-word costume (Search, Scan, Sample, Simulate) that usually names a different facet than the mechanism. charter:14 authorizes dropping S but no machinery makes that easy. Failure: the control-theory and ecology slots return 'Sample' and 'Scan', score poorly on distinctness as thin Search variants, and the two domains most likely to yield a structurally different operation are eliminated on a naming artifact.

claim: All three leading names are already bound to other concepts in this ecosystem, which is where the mnemonic criterion should be tested — logs, status lines, and spoken sentences.
evidence: `interscout` is a live plugin in this workspace ('Pre-session UXR participant research plugin. Dispatches parallel research agents…'), so 'scout report' and 'run a scout' are already spoken phrases meaning something else. 'Search' is the built-in `web_search` tool, producing sentences like 'the Search phase used search'. 'Select' is the router's job — `SelectionHints` drives per-turn model selection, so 'selection' already denotes model routing here. Failure is slow rather than sharp: months of ambiguous log lines and cross-repo docs where 'scout' means two things, plus verbal disambiguation every time the phase is named.

claim: The tournament scores candidates against the six phase *names* rather than against the members that already carry their load, so "semantic distinctness" cannot distinguish a new member from a duplicate — and the no-S null is scored as "absence of a phase" instead of "these five members already carry the load".
evidence: Three of Scout's seven emitted fields have named carriers today: outward/lateral search is already granted to Orient/Decide/Act (`internal/tool/builtin.go:19-22`, `webPhases := []Phase{PhaseOrient, PhaseDecide, PhaseAct}`); "falsifiable prediction" + "reversible probe" is the existing experiment trio (`init_experiment`/`run_experiment` gated to Act, `log_experiment` to Act+Reflect, `internal/tool/builtin.go:33-51`); and the evidence schema already carries `Hypothesis`, `Decision`, `Delta` for that lifecycle (`internal/agent/deps.go:90-96`). Retrieval of prior-session lessons is carried by Orient via `quality_history` (`internal/tool/builtin.go:25-29`).

claim: The `Reflect → Compound → Scout ⇢ Observe` topology draws a tenon into a mortise that does not exist: the phase FSM is a forward-only cursor with no back-edge, and the arrow's target phase (Observe) is the one phase the CLI refuses to start.
evidence: `internal/agent/phase.go:39-47` — `Advance()` only increments an index and errors past the end; no `Goto`, no back-edge; `IsTerminal()` is "at Compound" (`:49-52`). `cmd/skaffen/main.go:216-221` validates `--phase` against orient/decide/act/reflect/compound and rejects `observe` outright; the flag help omits it (`:55`) and the `--model` fan-out skips it (`:160`).

claim: The charter's most consequential question — phase vs side-loop vs capability vs artifact type — is posed with no test, though this frame makes the test mechanical: in Skaffen a phase *is* a capability gate, so the discriminator is the gate delta.
evidence: `PHILOSOPHY.md:13`: OODARC phases "aren't just workflow labels — they're hard security boundaries" enforced by the tool registry; enforcement lives in `defaultGates` (`internal/tool/registry.go:48-72`). Scout's gate delta against Orient is empty: Orient already grants read/glob/grep/ls (`registry.go:53-55`) plus web_search/web_fetch (`builtin.go:19-22`) plus quality_history (`builtin.go:25-29`).

claim: Scout is pinned at the wrong end of the beam: placed after the phase that cuts the session's durable artifact, while two of its three stated triggers (unresolved contradiction, detected shear) surface during Orient.
evidence: `internal/agent/agent.go:246-253` runs `mutations.Aggregate` and writes the quality signal when phase == Compound; the only reader of that artifact is Orient in a *later* session via `quality_history` (`internal/tool/builtin.go:25-29`, `internal/tool/quality_history.go:17-31`). Anything Scout emits after Compound cannot influence the artifact the frame carries forward.

claim: "Complexity cost: earns a new letter rather than adding taxonomy" is the only tournament criterion with no unit, so it will lose every close call to criteria with vivid ones — yet the cost is exactly countable as re-cut sites.
evidence: A seventh phase requires re-cuts at ten sites minimum: `internal/agent/phase.go:10-17` (+ `IsTerminal` at `:49-52`); `internal/tool/tool.go:48-53` (constants) and `:56-60` (legacy alias block — the five aliases brainstorm/plan/build/review/ship are still documented as the phase FSM at `AGENTS.md:9`); `internal/tool/registry.go:48-72` (omitting a `defaultGates` entry silently grants zero tools); `internal/router/router.go:21-26`; `internal/router/shadow.go:26-42` (two maps); `cmd/skaffen/main.go:55`, `:160`, `:216-221`, `:514`; `internal/session/session.go:85-101` (per-phase prompt guidance) — plus the phase-gate matrix tests `AGENTS.md:60` requires. The capability form costs one site (`RegisterForPhases(NewScoutTool(), []Phase{PhaseOrient})` in `builtin.go`). The no-S null costs zero.

source_domains: hadith criticism / ilm al-rijal graded reliability

claim: The charter's central safety claim — "scout reports cannot become evidence directly" — is asserted and enforced by nothing, and the runtime it lands in has one ungraded store whose aggregate is read back by Orient, so any candidate that adds a writer without adding a grade field is net-negative against the no-S null.
evidence: Four automatic hops: (1) `agent.Evidence` has 25 fields and none is a grade, authority, or record id (`internal/agent/deps.go:61-96`); `JSONLEmitter` appends every event to one per-session file and best-effort bridges the same event to intercore (`internal/evidence/emitter.go:38-74`, `:130`). (2) Compound calls `mutations.Aggregate` (`internal/agent/agent.go:246-253`), which reads every line and silently `continue`s past any record it cannot unmarshal (`internal/mutations/aggregate.go:36-47`). (3) The output `QualitySignal` retains only session id, timestamp, phase, task type, and aggregate rates (`internal/mutations/signal.go:16-46`). (4) A later Orient turn reads it back through `quality_history` (`internal/tool/quality_history.go:17-31`, gated to Orient at `internal/tool/builtin.go:25-29`).

claim: Scout's "expiration or review condition" specifies demotion as a field on a document — no actor, no act, no store, no trigger — and the runtime makes it unenforceable: the only durable store is append-only and its records have no identifier to re-grade against.
evidence: `internal/evidence/emitter.go:54-74` — `appendJSONL` opens with `O_APPEND|O_CREATE|O_WRONLY` and syncs, so a record cannot be edited in place; `internal/agent/deps.go:61-96` — `Evidence` has no id field, so a compensating "re-grade" record would have nothing to point at.

claim: The charter requires forward routing and never requires backward traceability, so the chain terminates at promotion: a compounded lesson keeps no link to probe, report, or source domain, and discrediting a link can never trigger re-grading.
evidence: Promotion is `mutations.Aggregate` (`internal/agent/agent.go:246-253`), which reduces N records to sums and rates (`internal/mutations/aggregate.go:60-68`) and writes a `QualitySignal` whose provenance fields are exactly session id, timestamp, phase, task type (`internal/mutations/signal.go:16-25`). No record ids, no probe reference, no source domain.

claim: The Falsifiability criterion scores whether a candidate produces probes, not whether a probe's failure is recorded against the source-domain analogy that motivated it, so a source domain's tenth failed borrowing is indistinguishable from its first.
evidence: `ExperimentEvent` records `Type`, `Campaign`, `Hypothesis`, `Decision`, `Delta` (`internal/agent/deps.go:90-96`) — a complete local outcome record with no field naming where the hypothesis came from.

source_domains: hadith criticism / ilm al-rijal graded reliability

claim: The two fields that make Scout look rigorous — correspondence mapping and where-the-analogy-breaks — carry no validity test: no shared effective cause need be named, and nothing bars transferring from a source claim that is itself ungraded, so the grade attaches to the act of scouting rather than to the strength of the chain behind the claim.
evidence: A correspondence mapping as specified is satisfied by listing paired nouns; a mechanism read off a blog post and a mechanism established in the system's own compounded record enter Scout on identical terms and leave carrying the same `authority: speculative` (charter:38). The runtime has no source-grade field to inherit from anyway (`internal/agent/deps.go:61-96`).

claim: Claim (1) holds as the defect of record and claim (2) is demoted from rival defect to binding runtime constraint: (2) presupposes an outcome measure that (1) correctly observes is never named, so an unspecified pilot has no measure to confound - but (2)'s strongest form is broader than stated, because 'read-only' fails under BOTH its operational and its epistemic readings.
intersection_justification: The adjudication itself: resolving the (1)-vs-(2) contradiction required grounding both in the runtime, which surfaced that the disputed word 'read-only' has two undisambiguated senses and that (2)'s mechanism holds under the sense it did not invoke.
evidence: Item 7 in full is eleven words with no dependent variable: 'A minimal read-only pilot for the top two choices plus the no-S null.' Claim (2) reaches its conclusion only by imputing QualitySignal as the outcome, because that is the only aggregate the runtime produces - an imputation that is a repair of (1), which makes (2) conditional on (1) being fixed first. The charter never defines 'read-only', and its own line 41 ('scout reports cannot become evidence directly') invites the epistemic reading. Operational reading fails at internal/agentloop/loop.go:286, where `l.emitter.Emit(ev)` sits unconditionally in the turn body, gated on nothing. Epistemic reading fails at internal/agent/agent.go:246-253, where mutations.Aggregate runs on the Compound phase over the WHOLE session file, so a never-promoted scout turn still moves Hard.TurnCount (aggregate.go:73), Hard.TokenEfficiency (:66-72) and Soft.ToolErrorRate (:85); internal/mutations/signal.go:17-18 states the signal is 'Written by the Compound phase, read by Orient on subsequent sessions'. Decidable, not a taste call: the two claims are ordered (specification, then feasibility), not in tension.

claim: If item 7 is repaired the obvious way and uses the quality signal as its outcome, the two pilot arms are written to different files and never compared: a minimal read-only pilot session is by construction no-write/no-edit/read-heavy, which is exactly inferTaskType's first branch, routing it to docs.jsonl while the no-S null arm routes to feature/bug-fix/refactor.
intersection_justification: Exposed only by adjudicating the two claims together: (1)'s 'cannot lose' and (2)'s confounding turn out to be two faces of one missing dependent variable, and tracing (2)'s mechanism into store.go revealed the arms never share a file at all. EMERGENT: both parent findings (f-006, f-007) sit at :119 but neither connected the missing outcome variable to task-type bucketing; the per-type file split is in neither.
evidence: internal/mutations/aggregate.go:133 opens with `case !hasWrite && !hasEdit && hasGrep: return TaskDocs` - a read-only scout pilot session matches that branch exactly. internal/mutations/store.go:89-95 (taskTypeFile) and :97-129 (WriteForType) then append the signal to `<tasktype>.jsonl`, and Orient reads per-type (signal.go:17-18), so the S arm and the null arm accumulate in separate histories and are never scored against one another. Compounding it, QualitySignal.Scores() penalizes turn count and rewards tokens_out/tokens_in: adding an S phase strictly adds turns, and scout turns are read-heavy, so token efficiency falls too - any S candidate loses on both axes for reasons unrelated to transfer quality. This is the exact mirror of settled finding (1): item 7 as written cannot lose; item 7 as a reader would implement it cannot win.

source_domains: control theory, cybernetics, and OODA loop doctrine

claim: CONFIRMED, and wider than claimed: the mechanism-to-word substitution is enforced not only by the S-word seeds and the mnemonic criterion but by the box-shaped per-candidate spec, which makes the charter's own mandated control-theory candidate class structurally unenterable, and the substitution cost is never required to be declared.
evidence: Every element of the prior finding checks out: :12 poses a word-slot question; :53-61 lists nine seeds, eight of them S-verbs; :68 requires a 'control theory or cybernetics' candidate; :95 makes 'concise, verb-shaped, pronounceable' a tournament criterion and :96 denominates cost in letters; :111-119 contains no output item asking which loop edges change; :14 permits dropping the letter but never requires reporting what the letter excluded. Strengthening: the primitives the cybernetics slot at :68 actually offers are edge modifiers, not boxes - a dead-band/hysteresis on the Reflect-to-Compound promotion gate, a variety amplifier on Orient's input channel, a change of loop gain or sampling window. None has an input/output contract, a re-entry path, or a phase/side-loop answer, yet :76, :79 and :83 demand exactly those of every serious candidate, so that class can only be entered by impersonating a phase. The runtime confirms the excluded class is the load-bearing one: the sole cross-session learning edge is internal/agent/agent.go:246-253 -> internal/tool/builtin.go:27-28 (quality_history gated to PhaseOrient only) -> internal/session/session.go:179 (ReadRecent(5)), and its only two tunable control parameters are the promotion gate and the 5-sample window - neither proposable under the current spec schema.

source_domains: control theory, cybernetics, and OODA loop doctrine

claim: The runtime's only outcome measure has no dimension in which exploration can pay off within the window Orient reads, so the charter's falsifiable pilot returns a negative verdict on any S candidate regardless of whether it works.
evidence: QualitySignal.Scores() (internal/mutations/signal.go:52-70) is monotone against exploration: token_efficiency higher-better, -turn_count, -tool_error_rate, -tool_denial_rate, approval_rate, outcome. internal/mutations/aggregate.go:63-70 computes TokenEfficiency as totalOut/totalIn across the whole session, so scouting turns dilute it directly; Orient reads a five-session moving average (internal/session/session.go:179) and internal/mutations/best.go:9 Pareto-selects over the same one-sided vector across 50 signals. No field records cross-domain transfer. Meanwhile the tournament criteria have the mirror defect: Generativity (:93) rewards exploration and nothing in :89-96 prices it - Complexity cost (:96) counts letters, not turns. Failure scenario: the item-7 pilot runs ~10 sessions, every scouted session shows lower TokenEfficiency and higher TurnCount, no session can show a transfer benefit because no field carries one, and the pilot reports 'Scout degrades quality' - the identical result it would produce for a Scout that worked perfectly.

source_domains: control theory, cybernetics, and OODA loop doctrine

claim: The charter makes pace/shear fit a structural tournament criterion but names no pace layer that exists in the runtime, so the criterion cannot separate any two candidates and collapses into a tiebreaker.
evidence: :27 asserts 'coupled loops at multiple pace layers rather than one mandatory linear turn sequence' and :92 scores 'natural cadence and cross-layer behavior', yet no layer is named anywhere in the charter. The runtime carries exactly two cadences, neither mentioned: the per-turn agentloop inside a single phase (internal/agent/agent.go:230-241) and the per-session outer edge whose lag constant is the literal 5 in ReadRecent(5) (internal/session/session.go:179). grep -ri 'pace|cadence' over internal/ returns no OODARC-related hit. The FSM is strictly linear and one-way - fixed phaseOrder, Advance() only, IsTerminal() at Compound (internal/agent/phase.go:10-50) - so 'coupled loops' describes an intention rather than the artifact being reviewed. Every candidate will therefore score identically on an undefined scale.

source_domains: control theory, cybernetics, and OODA loop doctrine

claim: The charter requires an expiration or review condition of every scout report but requires none of its own recommendation, so the review is an open-loop controller change with no feedback path back to itself.
evidence: :39 makes 'expiration or review condition' a mandatory field of the low-authority scout report. Item 5 at :117 asks only for 'a recommendation with confidence and explicit conditions under which it changes' - the conditions are unconstrained, need not be observable in any artifact the runtime emits (internal/evidence/emitter.go or mutations.QualitySignal), and carry no revisit date or cycle count. The decay term is imposed on the governed artifact and omitted from the governing one, which is the higher-authority write into the architecture.

source_domains: control-flow archaeology of a running FSM

claim: Finding (2) holds and dissolves finding (1): Skaffen's phaseFSM carries no control flow at all — it is an integer index advanced only by a human `/advance` slash command — so a phase reduces to a named capability profile, the gate delta is the discriminator, and Scout's required capability set is a strict subset of Orient's (delta = ∅). The missing backward edge that (1) objects to is a category error, not a defect, because no automatic forward edge exists either.
intersection_justification: The contradiction only resolves by reading control flow rather than the charter: (1) is a code-shaped claim about a missing FSM edge, (2) is a semantics-shaped claim about what a phase means. Fusing them required finding the single caller of AdvancePhase, which shows the FSM has no automation at all — a fact neither prior finding had, and which makes (1) moot while confirming (2)'s premise in corrected form.
evidence: internal/agent/phase.go:9-51 — phaseOrder is a fixed six-element slice, phaseFSM is an int index, Advance() does f.index++ and errors past Compound; no Reset, no SetPhase, no reverse edge (so (1) is factually right). internal/tui/commands.go:196-213 — the ONLY non-test caller of AdvancePhase() is the `/advance` TUI command; there is no automatic forward transition, so the charter's `Reflect → Compound → Scout ⇢ Observe` at :44 describes a machine that exists in neither direction. internal/agent/agent.go:88 — default FSM start is tool.PhaseAct, not Observe. internal/tool/registry.go:48-70 + internal/tool/builtin.go:19-22,25-29 — effective gates are Observe {read,glob,grep,ls}; Decide = Observe ∪ {web_search,web_fetch}; Orient = Decide ∪ {quality_history}. Scout (:31, 'searches related, lateral, and orthogonal domains') needs read/grep/glob + web_search/web_fetch — a STRICT SUBSET of Orient. internal/router/router.go:19-27 — phaseDefaults maps all six phases to ModelOpus, so the router axis discriminates nothing; SelectModel (:78-84) falls through to ModelSonnet with reason 'fallback-default' on an unknown phase, so declaring PhaseScout without editing phaseDefaults silently DOWNGRADES the charter's most generative phase. internal/tool/web_search.go:75-86 — tierForPhase (Orient→deep, Decide→auto, Act→instant) is the only place phase does work beyond gating, and the charter specifies nothing on that axis. Why (1) loses: its objection is contingent on ~10 lines (phaseOrder is a slice; a Reset() or newPhaseFSM(PhaseObserve) restores the cycle), and a missing edge in a hand-driven index is not evidence about the conceptual question; (2)'s objection survives any amount of Go, since a gate delta of ∅ closes only by inventing a capability Orient lacks, and the charter names none.

source_domains: control-flow archaeology of a running FSM

claim: Pointed symmetrically, the gate-delta discriminator indicts the incumbents: Observe ⊂ Decide ⊂ Orient is a strict 1-2 tool nesting under identical model routing with no enforceable transition, so three of six existing phases fail the 'semantic distinctness' and 'operational crispness' criteria the charter applies to challengers — every ranking against the unexamined no-S baseline is therefore uninterpretable, and the honest recommendation space must include 'merge existing phases'.
intersection_justification: Emerged only from adjudicating the dispute — accepting (2)'s discriminator obliges turning it on the baseline, which neither original finding did, and the result inverts the charter's addition-only framing.
evidence: internal/tool/registry.go:50-58 + internal/tool/builtin.go:19-22,27 — Observe {read,glob,grep,ls} ⊂ Decide (+web_search,web_fetch) ⊂ Orient (+quality_history): strict set nesting. The entire runtime content of 'Orient vs Decide' is one tool (quality_history, Orient-only) plus one Exa tier string (deep vs auto, internal/tool/web_search.go:76-86). internal/router/router.go:20-26 — all six phases route to ModelOpus, zero routing delta. internal/tui/commands.go:196 — the sole transition mechanism is a human typing `/advance`, so no phase has an enforceable state transition. Orient and Decide thus score near-zero on :89 'minimal overlap with O/O/R/C' and zero on :90 'enforceable input/output and state transition' — the exact grounds on which any S candidate would be rejected. This extends rather than repeats the settled fact that no-S scores N/A on most criteria: the sharper problem is not that the null is unscorable but that the incumbents, when scored, fail.
